title: Has potential, but needs more features no greater customisation
body:
I have ADHD so I fit the primary target demographic. 

PiCal appears to be only a new front end to apple calendars. It presents information graphically in variable time blocks and adds limited check list functionality.

I like the application as it has potential, but in my opinion is not worth even a fraction of the asking price. 

For me to buy this application it would need at least the following additional features:
(1) Ability to nominate start day of the week (Sunday, not Monday)
(2) Ability to edit checklists (without having to delete entire event)
(3) multiple checklists — one for task breakdowns and at least one more for what equipment, chemicals etc., that I should take for work at that location on that particular day
(4) I want to be able to populate my schedule for say every Monday but would want to be able to easily modify checklists for 1st, 2nd, 3rd. 4th and 5th week of the month etc. 
(5) Additional fields similar to location field. I want to be able to record phone numbers and other contact information for people I should contact at that location. Perhaps this could be a simple link to contacts …

title: Brilliant design for ADHD people
body:
Time blindness is the term for having an impaired sense of time—how long things take, how much time has passed, or how much time is available. This leads to chronic lateness, task mismanagement, and difficulty with future planning or urgency.

A 24h (vs 12h) clock face is an ingenious way of visually seeing time. It externally signals what a time-blind person can’t intuitively grasp.  

Cognitively it’s understood but it remains just an abstraction. It doesn’t change behaviour.  

Visualising two tracks of time blocks represented over the whole 24h period is simply brilliant.

title: In Love, I'll never use a different calendar again
body:
I absolutely love PICAL and as I have ADHD I don't want to use any other calendar. I adore it, especially having it on my Apple Watch and not depending on my phone anymore to track my time, or see upcoming tasks of the day. I really really appreciate it. It has helped so so much with time blindness it makes me happy.
I'll write a more detailed review soon as some of the functions of PiCal are so rare it would be useful for people to whon how PiCal is different especially if your brain is different and other calendars don't work for you!

Update September 2024 Honestly I have so many things in my to do list but I need to come leave an updated review because this app is now centre of my routine and it has made my life easier in so many ways. 

Yes it's been working for me. I use Asana for my business/calendar/tasks and I sync asana with google calendar. Then I also have google calendar synced with Weel (former Pical) and so I see all my tasks on my apple watch with the weel widget. Game changer. 

The gadget allows me to just plainly look at time in a different way. I no longer check my watch to see what time it is, I check my watch to see how long I have until my next task, or how long I still have for what I'm working on. Completely ADHD friendly, finally someone who gets it! I don't care about what time it is I just want to know how long I have! My anxiety has gone down, my productivity has gone up, I feel more present on any activity because timeblindness is not ruining mylife. I still love Asana for my project management so I can run my business like that and use Weel as my daily calendar. 

Every day I look at my asana calendar and add on weel the tasks with starting and ending time exactly as I want to plan my day, and that's it. I love this routine. The watch is also super motivating in other aspects so it's the gadget that keeps on track with almost everything. From drinking water to exercice to completing my to do list to being on time. I feel like Weel has allowed me to merge all the little things I needed to create the perfect routine that is making me happy right now. I can run my business, I can be present with my son, I can commute/travel with ease. Really saying this app is great is an understantement, I hope lots of people download it and give it a try because it can actually change your life.

title: Actually represents time in an ADHD-friendly way
body:
I'm in the trial period, so I have a few days to decide whether to purchase a subscription, but here are my thoughts so far.

I have been looking so long for something that will tell me how long it is until the next event that I've been seriously considering learning Xcode/Swift so I could write my own application.  My ADHD brain looks at "appointment at 15:30" and just shrugs. I then have to check the current time, and do some mental math.. which is just enough effort that I'm likely to simply make a bad assumption about how long I have instead, and anyway the whole process just needlessly adds mental friction when all I ever want to know is how long until the thing. This app will tell you "2h 20m". Yes! No mental effort needed to interpret, no additional information to look up. I know how long I have. And the widgets and watch complications represent time this way as well. Perfect.

Another positive: the wheel. It does just make more sense to me. It's easier to scan and understand where I am and how much time various things will take. And it's nice for time blocking because you can just move stuff around the circle when you get off track and need to push some things until later. AND it actually updates the entries in your actual calendar when you update them on the circle (except in one case, which I'll mention in a moment). Oh, and you can "dim" calendars that you still want to see but that aren't vital to you.

I tried using a similar app with a round interface, Owaves, and loved it. Its UI was definitely smoother, but it was a complete walled garden with no way to sync events to other calendars and they were trying to push people to use it as social media, which makes me suspicious that they're just going to end up funding it with your data. I prefer Pical's approach.

And regarding the privacy aspect: there's no account to sign up for, the dev claims not to collect your data, it uses calendars you already have (for me that's my iOS and Nextcloud calendars), so you keep control of your data while it keeps itself synced across your devices. Excellent.

Those are some major positives.  Here are the negatives:
- The widgets and interface don't automatically change with system dark/light mode. The light mode is easier to read, but at night a bright screen is a problem for me, so I have to keep manually turning it on and off. Annoying.
- If you create an event in the app you can't assign it to a calendar, so it will only ever appear in the app and not on your other calendars. If you want an event to sync, you have to create it elsewhere.
- The wheel is shaded between 6am and 6pm for night time/day time, and you can't change it. For me that time is completely arbitrary, so it only adds distracting visual noise. It would be better to leave out the shading until the ability to customise it is added.
- Sometimes moving events and deleting events can be glitchy. I assume this is from the overhead needed to update your external calendars as well, but it makes the app feel a bit clunky.
- Price. It's kind of spendy. On the one hand, I prefer to pay developers so they don't need to monetize via data mining. But they're charging 3 times the cost of Fantastical for a subscription. It's a bit much.

Mitigating these negatives is the fact that the developer has the roadmap on their website, and the app appears to be getting at least a couple of updates a month, so it's actively being worked on. All in all I'm thrilled that someone is actually making a calendar app tailored to my brain, and I'm hopeful that it will continue to get improvements.

body: The things that you’re offering like different colored events does not in any way warrant a subscription! I don’t care if it’s only 5 a month, this is one time purchase stuff at best. Nothing you’re offering requires constant maintenance on your end, like if you were to provide a cloud based service of your own. This app requires none of that from you, and so why do you ask us to pay you regularly??? Quit being greedy!
author: AlissUnknown

title: Best Calendar App
body: The Smartest visualization of your day’s activities/habits and meetings in a 24hr clock/circular format.  A refreshing take on your time, in a calendar & todo app in one hybrid. Worth a look for sure.
author: oliverlestrange

title: I really want this to work but I hate it.
body: The wheel format for the day is exactly what I want. But the only way to make this app work is to allow full access to my calendar and any event I put in Weel gets added to my actual calendar too. I share my calendar with my husband and I wanted a scheduling app that’s JUST FOR ME FOR MY OWN DAY. it won’t allow me to add any event that’s not tied to my calendar and I freaking hate that. If you don’t allow full access or any access to calendars, it won’t even let you add any event to your schedule. Those should be optional features. Good grief.
author: LaneTheLee

title: Maybe we need something different
body: I’ve been struggling to find anything that will help me orient myself to time. I have been using this for a few days, and I still have some ways to go in implementing it. However, for the first time I can see myself identifying lapses in a day between calendar events and logging what I have actually done. That evidence is helpful in understanding what does and does not work. I’m currently sitting at a restaurant and saw the dial post to 7pm. it helped me understand I have two more hours before the time I would typically want to crawl in bed and read a book (when I’m not working late nights bc dopamine surge). So, I was able to think.. how do I want to spend it? All of this to say, thanks for helping me feel a flash of hope. Would really love to connect with the developers to see how I can make this stick.
author: portiapreston

title: my favorite app
body: I honestly really love the weel app!! I take any opportunity to talk about this app to everyone I am friends with. I have used weel every single day of my undergrad experience, but I was really worried about being able to afford it now that I have started graduate school. The team was so kind and sent me a discount code for the year that will seriously make such a big difference!!!! I am eternally grateful and I love this app even more now. Sometimes there are some little bugs and glitches but I love this app too much to complain. 💗
author: itsyazzzmin

title: Great concept, poorly executed
body: I accepted the free trial to have access to the “premium” features, which are really just basic features like repeating events, so you’re forced to subscribe, and immediately realized this app isn’t worth a dime. Upon setting up my first event, work, I noticed that “travel time” is only accounted for at the beginning of the event. Apparently at the end of the event you just teleport home. Second thing I noticed is that there’s no option for an event to repeat a couple times a week, it’s either every weekday or you’re creating a new event for each day. These two issues right away signaled that this is just a money grab and isn’t thought through in the least bit. It’s 2026, apps aren’t THAT hard to create these days. Basic functionality shouldn’t be this bad.

I fr think this app has potential for someone like me who has ADHD but it's not worth a $149 life time subscription. A bit bold of a price for something that seems very half baked.

title: LOVE THIS APP!
body:
This app changed my life!!! It’s the best calendar I’ve had to organize my life. I love how the face is 24 hours and I can easily add appointments. I can also easily check what time it will be in my time zone when friends from abroad ask to schedule appointments. I love how I can add transit options (walking, biking or driving) so my calendar tells me exactly when to leave. I’m a fan of how many color options I can use for different appointments and how easy it was (and still is) to sync my other calendars with this one once I downloaded it. My wife has the same app and we can easily sync our appointments. 

Most of the complaints about this app have been bug fixes that are now fixed. I’m happy to pay for an app that doesn’t sell my information or I am not the product they are selling. Thank you for creating such a great app that helps to keep my life organized!

author: Oddomission

title: This is the app I have been searching for
body:
Update: I am happy to report that I have continued using the app to great effect. The glitch I reported in my earlier review was the result of user error. As I’ve become more comfortable using the app, I realized I simply did not notice that you sometimes need to scroll up/down to see your text when writing notes. When opening notes, they don’t always generate where you left off. 
However, I have a fresh request. I have created a recurring daily “diary” task to track my progress. After a week of work, I realized that the edits I made erased my earlier notations (at times, I see an option to select “Save for this event” v. “save for future events,” but this does not appear reliably and it shows up on the bottom of my screen in a place where it is very difficult for me to click on it (I can only see half a line of the text at a time, if at all. I need to scroll up/down to choose and option and because this appears at the bottom of the screen, my IPad thinks I intend to close the app instead.)
I would love to see a diary option added to the interface so that I no longer need to create an event for it every day. I would also love for this/any notes to have a search function that will allow me to easily pull up when I had a meeting with a specific person or when we discussed a specific event. 

All-in-all, this is the best app I have found to assist with my complex executive functioning deficits. As an autistic person working in a professional administrative position, this app is a life saver. I am intensely grateful for the work that was put into this.

I have been looking for an app that combined Reminders (with check lists), a visual clock like the Wakka app, and Notes into one. I usually use all my tech in dark mood. However, I cannot see the text when writing notes for the day in dark mode. If this is not simply a glitch, then I feel they should not charge a subscription fee to use Light mode. Please update this note taking feature.

I definitely love the widgets and I can see myself keeping this app just for that, regardless of whether the above suggestions are implemented. I plan to also use this to help plan out my trips into town, so I can better see my bus/timing options

title: Little kinks make it difficult
body:
I really like this app but I wish it had a few more features. 

I wish there was an option for weekdays or weekends so I can more easily set up routines. Maybe the reoccurring option would allow you to pick the days they reoccur? Like a Tues, Thurs, reoccurring event is a little challenging to add. Plus you can’t copy/paste events. For someone who has the “out of sight/out of mind” ADHD, this tool becomes more challenging than helpful in this area. I also wish there was an “all day busy” feature that I could see on the pi chart so I could see that I can’t schedule anything on a day. I tried doing something similar by doing 12am-11:55pm but it leaves a really annoying little sliver that I can’t stop staring at. Also, I need to be able to schedule multiple reminders (like 10) for some things. So more opportunity for reminders are helpful. 

I know this is being advertised for people with ADHD but the app still feels very neurotypical to be honest.

author: daviddavini

title: Crashes before I can even set it up
body:
It seems like it’d be a cool app, but it’s hard to say cuz it crashes the second after I set up the first scheduled event (I couldn’t find a way to get into the app without setting one up.) When setting up the first event, I was unable to see what I was typing in the “location” box cuz the keyboard covers it completely and doesn’t allow you to scroll down so it’s visible above the keyboard. Then after I had set up all the features of it I wanted, it wouldn’t allow me to continue until I added it to one of my ical calendars i had allowed it to sync with (family, personal, medical, etc.) but the first time, it only gave me 2 choices, both of which were “read-only” calendars I had imported from my kid’s school and scout troop. Except they were both greyed-out and unable to be chosen, and you can’t move on without choosing one. I forget how I eventually got around that (it wasn’t ideal but I planned to try to go back and edit it once it had been created) but regardless, within a second of creating the event, the app crashed and every time I tried to reopen it, it would crash again.

Ok, fine. I’ve already agreed to the 7-day free trial, so I uninstalled and redownloaded it, went through the whole process again. This time I created the event with a different ring, and I’m not sure why that made a difference (since I hadn’t been able to explore the app at all cuz you can’t do that until you create an event) but this time I still had to add the event to one of my iCal synced calendars. It was only giving me 2 options out of about 6 or 7, but I just picked one, again planning to update/edit it after it was created, but then it just kept crashing again.

At this point, as I said, I have already begun the 7-day trial, and even if these other issues somehow got resolved, I’d be curious to see how that could get fixed as well so I could actually have a fair chance to try it before having to pay a subscription to even see if I like it. For the time being, I’ll be canceling the subscription so I don’t forget to cancel it before it autocharges me the monthly fee in 6 days. 

I’d be happy to amend this review if/when these issues are resolved and I’m able to give an actual review of the app itself instead of just reviewing my inability to even test drive it.

title: App support missing?
body: Love the design. I cannot find any FAQ or support info to help understand the app and features.
author: Jethro7274

title: Nice start
body: The phone app and Widgets are alright and so as advertised. But the Watch feature needs work. I have all my calendars set up in the app and they work flawlessly with the widget and display everything. But the Watch portion still complains that it needs access to my calendars… there’s nothing in the app that tells me anything about the Watch or that there’s even a Watch feature… I’d love to use it on my watch if it ever works. And there definitely needs to be better ui involved
author: kodama52

title: Pie calendar doesn’t show on the Apple Watch
body: It just shows the listed items on my apple calendar. Nothing more at all. I wasted my time on trying to figure things out. It didn’t have trouble linking to my calendar and I had to figure out to fix that issue! Let me tell you this is not my first download of any productivity or calendar app at all. I’m avid users of different calendar or schedule apps. I’ve never had any issues using with any Apple Watch app until today. I’ve been using Apple Watch since 2017. They should’ve updated timely as the Apple iOS updated and released, and if there’s any issues at the time, they should have mentioned them and how to deal with them in the app description section.
author: miiiwaaa-

title: None of my events are showing on the Display
body: Sounds like a Great app but u havent been able to use it as intended on download. Iphone 13 Ios 15.0.2. Also input delay and chopped transitions on everything :(
author: D.T.25

title: Great Idea for Time Management
body: Loved the Idea of this app for time management. By one look I can see all the tasks and event in the month and locate the free time to utilize it efficiently which is great.   I hope in the next update the ability to give any event a certain color will be added, this will help help me to sort out the event and differentiate between them. Regards,
author: Alidki

title: Too obtuse
body:
Grabbed this for time tracking/management.

It too obtuse to even VIEW my calendars, much less MANAGE my time.

Doesn’t display correctly in landscape mode.

Also, WAY too expensive.
author: andcheese

title: Can’t add events
body: How is it that I am unable to add new events in this app… the app is completely non functional and then on top of that it’s laggy on my iPhone 11!
author: @faketextquotes IG

title: Great simple visual calendar
body:
I have a hard time keeping track of time on a digital clock, this is so helpful for tracking my day and meetings visually.

I especially love the widget! It’s so helpful for the way my brain works to easily SEE time passing.  I’m looking forward to more updates!
author: heathersabrina

title: Great visual calendar
body: This is a great visual calendar that helps me organize my days! I am even able to keep track of multiple calendars!
author: RedPanda Joey

title: Ooh, I could get into this...
body: Helpful to see the way different calendar items overlap in a 24 hour circle. Appreciate that it displays my already-existing calendar items (was able to just check boxes to include or exclude entire calendars). Very intuitive.
author: JessMcD

title: Useful visualization!
body: Helps me find time where my boss and I are both available. Also useful to find open meeting times with the part of my team that is located in Asia!
author: Nashdecker

title: A Revelation!
body:
Imagine putting on glasses and seeing for the first time, or switching on a hearing aid and hearing for the first time. That's what it felt like coming across Weel it grounds me in time!

Time makes sense with Weel.
